newsitem.title: CHINA: China interest levels appropriate - central bank.
newsitem.headline: China interest levels appropriate - central bank.

text.p: The People's Bank of China, the central bank, considers current interest rate levels to be appropriate after two rate cuts this year, the China Securities said on Monday.
China's macro-economic adjustments had achieved clear successes in 1996, the newspaper quoted a spokesman of the People's Bank as saying.
The bank now considered interest levels to be appropriate, it quoted the spokesman as saying in response to speculation that another rate cut was likely before the end of the year.

China cut interest rates in May and again in August in response to falling inflation. The most recent cut on August 23 trimmed bank deposit rates by an average of 1.5 percentage points and lending rates by 1.2 percentage points.
The two cuts had achieved their hoped-for results, the People's Bank spokesman said.

The cuts had sliced total interest payments by the nation's borrowers by 100 billion yuan ($12 billion), easing the debt burden on state enterprises. It said the move had also helped boost government revenues but gave no details.

The interest rate cuts had also helped keep the increase in M1 and M2 money supply close to state-set targets and had increased liquidity while helping in the management of commercial banks, China Securities quoted the spokesman as saying.
China's state-run banks have been struggling to stay profitable as their own cost of funds is high while many cash-strapped state enterprises have had trouble repaying debt.
